title: Poincare duality conventions: trace and trace-cup pairing
statement:
In the conventions of [def-pod-conventions] ($X_0$ not necessarily
proper), fix $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ and use the coefficient cohomology of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] and the Tate twists of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. The trace construction of [def-weil-poincare-trace-cup], read at this coefficient stage, uses the
canonical orientation $\eta_X$ to read the counit of $Ra_{X!}\dashv Ra_X^!$,

$$
\operatorname{tr}_X:H_c^{2d}(X,\Lambda(d))\longrightarrow\Lambda,
\qquad
\operatorname{tr}^{(-d)}_X:H_c^{2d}(X,\Lambda)\longrightarrow\Lambda(-d),
$$

the second being its untwisted form; neither uses properness (compare
[def-pur-smooth-trace] at $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$. The identification with its normalized smooth trace is [cor-pur-finite-stage-smooth-dualizing-complex]; for $\Lambda\in\{\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ the counit is the transported normalized integration map of [cor-pur-adic-and-rational-smooth-dualizing-complexes]). If $X_0$ is
proper, then use the canonical comparison $\kappa:Ra_{X!}\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_{X*}$ of [prop-weil-proper-compact-coincidence] at the chosen coefficient stage (at finite coefficients, the proper comparison in [cor-cbc-proper-coincidence]), so
$H_c^{2d}\cong H^{2d}$ and, writing $h=H^{2d}(\operatorname{Fib}_s\kappa)$, the ordinary-cohomology trace is $\operatorname{tr}^{(-d)}_X\circ h^{-1}$. This is the corresponding map $H^{2d}(X,\Lambda)\to\Lambda(-d)$ in the trace convention of [def-weil-poincare-trace-cup] (literally its displayed map when $\Lambda=\mathbf Q_\ell$); only
under this properness assumption is the trace–cup pairing
$\langle x,y\rangle_i=\operatorname{tr}^{(-d)}_X(x\smile y)$ on
$H^i(X,\Lambda)\times H^{2d-i}(X,\Lambda)$ of that definition read in
these conventions.
